note: D6 and D7 are two different errors that the matcher glued together: D6's r1 half (Aqlab min -> no min, A2 idafa) and D7 (snenha -> snanha, vocab tier 1). r2's 0915-19 is the same row as D7, so D6 is settled as the grammar row and D7 as the vocab row; do not count them as one. Chat policy used here: every one of Amal's typed model lines that differs from what he said is labelled kind A with signal chat-fix, with confidence lowered to low when her voice had approved (Perfect / Nice / Mm-hmm) - the merger may want to keep those apart from voice fixes. The ASR in this lesson drops a final -h even in Amal's own lines (12:45 ما تكسري for ma tekserih), writes kasaro/kasaru both as كسروا, and its Latin stretches (livil, lavit, yaref) are rough, so several D-rows rest on her chat lines. Nothing added: every other slip I saw (راي/رأيي, تغير/تغيرت, Program masculine, kam sawar, Zakarini, ma id zakar, aja min/على, نفس الـ امبارح, تصوريني/صوريني, bitsawri/بتتصوري) reads as ground both readers would have covered.

rulings.why: بتيت is not recoverable from the ASR; he asked a meta question whether it works with يوم, she said 'it doesn't go', then answered Yeah to his next 'وي بتيت' at 01:32; no wrong -> right pair can be read from the transcript (transcript hole), and inventing the intended word is not allowed.

Not a didn't-know: he had already translated her مطفي as 'off' himself at 02:07 ('Why am I off?'); ما تفي is the ASR spelling of مطفي (S4 at most) and his 02:12 question is about usage (can it be said of people), not the word's meaning; she taught nothing he had attempted and got wrong.

Her chat 'talaat illa tult' at 05:15 transcribes his time answer exactly as her 05:05 chat transcribed his correct date; 'هلات إلى 12' is the ASR mangling of talaate illa tult (tult heard as twelve); no voice signal, she moved straight on to the weather.

rulings.why: r1's grammar half is a real, distinct error; r2's half of this pair is the same row as D7 and is settled there, so this row is grammar A2 only.

بوت is a valid word for shoes (sheet 'sneakers / boots | Boat | بوت'); the formal-shoes instruction was drill framing that she left out when she repeated the prompt at 37:31, he produced كندرتك the moment she asked for 'the other shoes', and her chat accepts both 'kundartek? / boatek?' - not a wrong word.
الآن for ألوان is a dropped و inside a word he knows (sheet 'colors | Alwaan | ألوان') - a root-letter sound slip, S4 pronunciation, never vocab; she said 'very close' and he fixed it at once.
